card.name: Comma after "in any event" in drug labels
card.fires_on: The comma after "in any event" in the stock sentence about serum level determinations not being widely available. Weaker on verbs or adverbs right after a subject, such as "have", "were" or "always".

modes.label: Serum level boilerplate
modes.description: Comma after "in any event" in the sentence saying serum drug levels are not widely available and have no established role.
modes.example: Laboratory determinations of serum levels of irbesartan are not widely available, and such determinations have, in any event<<,>> no established role in the management of ir

modes.label: Auxiliary verb after subject
modes.description: A helping verb or adverb partway through a clause, before the main verb.
